summary: Blackjack Ridge lookout site in Mount Baker-Snoqualmie NF: 30-ft pole tower built 1935, Aircraft Warning Service 1942-43, abandoned about 1950, now gone.

facts.status_note: Tower gone; Willhite found a scattering of bolts, wires, metal, a stove pipe and a wood stove at the site

staffing.status: No fire lookout staff named in the FFLOS, firelookout.com or Washington Lookouts pages. An undated Switchbacks excerpt on Willhite's page says a work crew was preparing the lookout for year-round occupancy and that an older miner and his wife were to spend the winter there.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest)

visit.trail_note: Approach is an old road, now a trail, from a barricaded pull-out; Willhite calls the trip an adventure that is not for the average hiker

events.note: 30-foot pole tower with L-4 cab; Former Fire Lookout Sites gives 1935, Washington Lookouts gives c.1935
Panoramic photos taken from the site on August 25, 1935; Willhite says only one panoramic shows much terrain
Sources disagree: Former Fire Lookout Sites and firelookout.com say a shake cabin was built; Washington Lookouts and Willhite say the Aircraft Warning Service added a small storage building
Aircraft Warning Service station activated September 11, 1942 (Seattle Filter Center listed)
Aircraft Warning Service station deactivated October 16, 1943
Abandoned in 1950 per Former Fire Lookout Sites and firelookout.com; Willhite says around 1950
Registered with Former Fire Lookout Sites on February 12, 2020

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Former Fire Lookout Sites and firelookout.com say a shake cabin was built in 1942; Washington Lookouts and Willhite say the Aircraft Warning Service added a small storage building. The story reports both and does not choose between them.

sources.title: Blackjack Ridge Lookout Site - Mountain Loop Highway

notes_for_editor: Brief record checked: 1935 build, 2020 FFLOS registration and gone status hold up; no corrections. No access level recorded because no source says whether the site is open. No fire lookout staff are named in the FFLOS, firelookout.com or Washington Lookouts pages. Willhite's page quotes an undated Switchbacks excerpt that says a work crew prepared the lookout for year-round occupancy and that an older miner and his wife were to spend the winter there; the story does not name them. The 1942 use was Aircraft Warning Service, not fire lookout staffing. The 1942 structure is disputed (shake cabin vs storage building). Washington Lookouts quotes Kresek's inventory and Willhite's site visit is undated beyond 2014 photo captions. WebSearch budget for this turn was exhausted by other agents, so no further sources were added.
